tasks.title: Why Ice Floats
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a physics podcast. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: The structure of some molecules
options.B: The causes and consequences of a natural phenomenon
options.C: A survival strategy of animals in winter
options.D: A common result of climate change

questions.stem: What difference between water and most other substances does the speaker discuss?

options.A: Scientists understand the structure of water molecules well.
options.B: Water requires a lot of heat to change its temperature.
options.C: Water expands when it changes from liquid to solid.
options.D: Liquid water reflects a lot of sunlight.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention aquatic life?

options.A: To emphasize a difference between lakes where ice forms and lakes where it does not.
options.B: To explain the importance of the insulating effect of ice at the top of bodies of water.
options.C: To provide an example of a harmful effect of warming water temperatures.
options.D: To identify a curiosity that has puzzled scientists for centuries.

questions.stem: What difference between liquid water and ice does the speaker discuss at the end of the talk?

options.A: Ice temperatures change more quickly.
options.B: Ice can absorb more energy.
options.C: Ice is easier to see from space.
options.D: Ice reflects more light.

tasks.title: Leonardo da Vinci's Mechanical Knight
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the lecture?

options.A: To review Leonardo da Vinci's most famous artistic works
options.B: To explain how early machines led to modern robotics
options.C: To highlight a lesser-known achievement of Leonardo da Vinci
options.D: To describe technological advances during the Renaissance

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Leonardo's fascination with the human body?

options.A: To indicate his contributions to medical science
options.B: To point out a key influence on Leonardo's designs
options.C: To explain why he spent more time studying anatomy than engineering
options.D: To emphasize Leonardo's artistic skills

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about Leonardo's mechanical understanding?

options.A: It depended on help from other scientists.
options.B: It was shown only in his sketches.
options.C: It was advanced for his time.
options.D: It relied mainly on trial and error.

questions.stem: What attitude does the speaker express toward the reconstruction of "Leonardo's Robot"?

options.A: He is relieved that some design flaws were corrected.
options.B: He is happy that Leonardo's sketches were published.
options.C: He is doubtful of the artistic value of the robot.
options.D: He is impressed by what the robot could do.

tasks.title: Bird Migration
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a science podcast. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The impact of light pollution on different bird species
options.B: A comparison of navigational cues used by migratory birds
options.C: The impact of climate change on bird habitats
options.D: Bird migration and its associated challenges

questions.stem: How does a special protein in the eyes of some birds help them navigate?

options.A: It helps them determine the position of the stars.
options.B: It helps them look toward the Sun without injury.
options.C: It helps them see Earth's magnetic field.
options.D: It helps them sleep with their eyes open.

questions.stem: What does the speaker warn may cause imbalances in food webs?

options.A: A decrease in the population of migrating birds
options.B: Slight changes in the migratory paths of birds
options.C: Increases in the distances traveled by migrating birds
options.D: Decreases in the population of pests along migratory paths

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is a measure people can take to protect migrating birds?

options.A: Producing fewer carbon emissions during the migration season
options.B: Turning off unnecessary lights at night
options.C: Making food available to migrating birds
options.D: Offering shelter to migrating birds during harsh weather

options.A: The historical origins of Cubism
options.B: How Cubism changed the world of art
options.C: Some similarities between architecture and Cubist art
options.D: Some examples of Cubist paintings

options.A: To provide a visual example of Cubist techniques
options.B: To highlight the influence of coffee on European artists
options.C: To identify a painting on which two Cubist artists worked together
options.D: To identify a common subject in many Cubist paintings

options.A: It quickly became popular among the general public.
options.B: It was not received well by some critics.
options.C: It became a topic in music and literature.

tasks.title: The Psychology of Flow
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a psychology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The benefits of achieving flow
options.B: The role of feedback in flow
options.C: The challenges of finding flow-inducing activities
options.D: The concept and characteristics of flow

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention athletes and artists?

options.A: To explain the role of feedback in achieving flow
options.B: To suggest that not everyone can achieve flow
options.C: To highlight the connection of flow to success
options.D: To provide examples of individuals who often experience flow

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about people who regularly experience flow?

options.A: They often work in jobs that include easy tasks.
options.B: They enjoy a variety of activities.
options.C: They are often happier and more fulfilled.
options.D: They earn more money than people who do not experience flow.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is a challenge to achieving flow?

options.A: Finding individuals to provide feedback
options.B: Identifying activities that are a proper match with skill level
options.C: Avoiding boredom when a task becomes too easy
options.D: Working on multiple things at the same time

tasks.title: Renaissance Tapestry Weaving
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Renaissance paintings and sculptures?

options.A: To contrast them with a less well-known art form from the same period
options.B: To provide examples of collaborative art forms
options.C: To highlight the religious nature of Renaissance art
options.D: To assert their superiority over other forms of Renaissance art

questions.stem: According to the talk, what was a key advantage of tapestries over frescoes?

options.A: They were cheaper to produce.
options.B: They could be displayed in museums.
options.C: They were easier to transport.
options.D: They depicted more complex scenes.

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what sometimes happened to tapestries while being transported from one location to another?

options.A: They were used as insulation.
options.B: They were stolen.
options.C: They became damaged.
options.D: Their designs were copied by other artists.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the process of tapestry creation during the Renaissance?

options.A: It required fewer resources than other art forms.
options.B: It involved a collaborative effort among several artisans.
options.C: It was mainly practiced in religious settings.
options.D: It was more popular than painting.

tasks.title: Dynamic Mimicry
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a biology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The ways that a sea creature changes its appearance
options.B: The ways that predators react to surprising behaviors
options.C: The ways that different animals capture prey
options.D: The ways that different species use dynamic mimicry

questions.stem: Why does the speaker discuss the owl butterfly?

options.A: To point out a limitation of dynamic mimicry
options.B: To highlight a hunting technique used by owls
options.C: To distinguish between two kinds of mimicry
options.D: To explain how mimicry can confuse experienced researchers

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is a limitation of changing shape?

options.A: It sometimes does not result in the intended shape.
options.B: It is not enough by itself to protect an animal from a predator.
options.C: It requires a significant amount of time.
options.D: It can quickly make muscles become tired.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention balloons?

options.A: To describe the pattern on a butterfly's wing
options.B: To show how camera equipment was raised and lowered
options.C: To explain how certain cells function in the mimic octopus
options.D: To emphasize how flexible the flatfish's muscles are

tasks.title: Music and Eating
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a music podcast. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about the tempo of music during meals?

options.A: The tempo should be adjusted with the type of food being eaten.
options.B: More research is needed on the effects of the tempo on digestion.
options.C: Fast music can improve taste perception.
options.D: Eating with slow music is better for health than eating with fast music.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the pitch of music?

options.A: The pitch can be used to emphasize specific aspects of the taste of food.
options.B: The perception of the pitch can be affected by the type of food being eaten.
options.C: Higher-pitched music can cause people to eat more quickly.
options.D: Doctors recommend listening to high-pitched music while eating.

questions.stem: What is a criticism of using music to influence food perception?

options.A: It can reduce the quality of the dining experience.
options.B: It can increase the cost of dining.
options.C: It can have unpredictable results because of varying individual tastes.
options.D: It can reduce people's ability to judge food accurately.

questions.stem: What caused the increase of diners' ratings of some food at the restaurant mentioned by the speaker?

options.A: Playing popular music
options.B: A decrease in music volume
options.C: Ocean sounds
options.D: A change in the food's taste

tasks.title: Underwater Archaeology
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: An archaeological subfield
options.B: Artifacts found from Ancient Rome and Ancient Greece
options.C: The challenges of excavating Roman ruins
options.D: Preservation techniques for artifacts

questions.stem: What point does the speaker emphasize about the archaeological site at Ephesus?

options.A: It is located in present-day Greece.
options.B: Its artifacts are mostly pottery and jewelry.
options.C: It was partly conducted using underwater archaeology.
options.D: It contains artifacts from different civilizations.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about wood and textiles?

options.A: They don't deteriorate as quickly when submerged in water.
options.B: They are difficult to recover.
options.C: They were carried on ships from Europe to Africa.
options.D: They are more commonly found at Roman sites than Greek sites.

questions.stem: What did archaeologists learn from studying the Uluburun shipwreck?

options.A: Information about Greek boatbuilding techniques
options.B: Information about ancient excavation methods
options.C: Information about ancient trading
options.D: Information about the evolution of jewelry making

tasks.title: Organizational Agility
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a business class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a streaming media company?

options.A: It did not perform as well as expected.
options.B: It did not hire many employees.
options.C: It advertised its products online.
options.D: It achieved success by changing what it offered.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a clothing retailer?

options.A: It hired a celebrity to help design its products.
options.B: It made several risky decisions.
options.C: Its supply chain adapts to new fashions quickly.
options.D: Its stores are spread across a wide variety of locations.

questions.stem: What agile practice adopted by an industrial firm does the speaker mention?

options.A: Designing buildings that could serve many different functions
options.B: Changing strategic goals based on new research
options.C: Quickly responding to customer concerns
options.D: Having people from different departments work together

questions.stem: How did the industrial firm's employees react to the introduction of agile practices?

options.A: They opposed the loss of familiar roles.
options.B: They began to work harder.
options.C: They resisted rigid hierarchies.
options.D: They were enthusiastic about new training opportunities.

tasks.title: Isolation in Literature
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a literature class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What aspect of isolation in literature does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: How it impacts society at large
options.B: How it is represented through characters in novels
options.C: How it impacts readers' perceptions of a work
options.D: Why it appears so frequently throughout different works

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the creature in Frankenstein?

options.A: He finds solace only in nature.
options.B: He is considered a tragic figure in literature.
options.C: He is an outcast because of his appearance.
options.D: He is a common subject in studies of isolation in literature.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Moby Dick?

options.A: To illustrate how isolation can have tragic consequences in literature
options.B: To contrast different literary perspectives on isolation
options.C: To explain why authors may choose isolation as a theme

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about the character Jane Eyre?

options.A: Jane does not recognize that she has been isolated.
options.B: Jane manages to make friends at boarding school.
options.C: Jane has chosen to isolate herself.
options.D: Jane uses isolation to her advantage.

tasks.title: Blue-Ringed Octopus and Tetrodotoxin
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a biology class. Then answer the questions.

options.A: Both produce compounds with medical uses.
options.B: Both depend on bacteria to survive.
options.C: They have nervous systems.
options.D: They exhibit similar survival behaviors.

questions.stem: What does the speaker explain by mentioning sodium channels in nerve cells?

options.A: How the blood of the blue-ringed octopus is adapted to the animal's environment
options.B: How a venom works
options.C: How bacterial contamination can affect some products
options.D: How the blue-ringed octopus moves

questions.stem: How does the venom of the blue-ringed octopus affect its prey?

options.A: It causes the prey to lose blood.
options.B: It makes the prey confused.

tasks.title: Jacob Lawrence and the Migration Series
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What about Jacob Lawrence does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: The difficulties he faced during the Great Migration
options.B: A series of paintings that is representative of his work
options.C: How he was influenced by other African American painters
options.D: How his style changed during his career

questions.stem: What is the speaker's attitude toward The Migration Series?

options.A: Disappointed that it is not widely known today
options.B: Confused about the purpose of including many panels
options.C: Impressed by this accomplishment early in Lawrence's career
options.D: Surprised by the information that Lawrence provided in the captions

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Harriet Tubman?

options.A: To describe a method that Lawrence used to paint human figures
options.B: To emphasize Lawrence's involvement in social activism
options.C: To introduce a point about African Americans in Northern cities
options.D: To provide an example of an important African American figure that Lawrence painted

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about Jacob Lawrence's critics?

options.A: They thought a child had painted some of his artworks.
options.B: They believed that The Migration Series was his best work.
options.C: They did not value work that seemed less artistically advanced.
options.D: They did not appreciate his earliest paintings as much as his later ones.

tasks.title: Dormitory Quiet Hours and Laundry
tasks.instruction: Listen to an announcement in a university dormitory. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about quiet hours?

options.A: They change depending on the day of the week.
options.B: They were recently adjusted based on students' feedback.
options.C: Not all residents have been mindful of them.
options.D: Not everyone should be expected to know about them.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the laundry facilities in the dormitory?

options.A: The machines have been broken by objects in students' clothes.
options.B: The machines are available for use between eleven p.m. and eight a.m.
options.C: Students have complained about the machines' noise.
